about: The damage zoo: do all image AIs break the same way when damaged? Open image AIs drew the same doodle request while a growing share of the neurons in one part was switched off. Written by scripts/damage_zoo.py web; the pictures are on /plato/zoo.
how: In every layer of one part, a random share of the feed-forward neurons was switched off (the same ones at every step, plus more), with the same random start for every picture. The AI's own weights were never changed: the damage was undone after each picture.
judged: By eye: each AI's range runs from intact to where its pictures stop meaning anything, chosen from a first pass at 0 to 90%, in 11 pictures. For fun and not pre-registered; nothing was measured, so how each AI breaks is a description, not a statistic.
request: A quick simple doodle sketch of a chair, black marker on plain white, like a 20-second drawing, no text, no shading.

parts.language: the part that reads the words (its text encoder)
parts.drawing: the part that draws the picture

how_it_breaks.language: Forgets the request: sketches of strangers, then a murky photo.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Lines thicken into stripes, then into texture.

how_it_breaks.language: Loses the request: God becomes an ordinary man; a bird, a page of birds.
Keeps the request a long time, then draws strangers in bright colour.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Melts into a dark blur, then grey static.

how_it_breaks.language: Forgets the words and draws stock photos: smiling people, posters, skylines.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Falls apart stroke by stroke, like a drawing being rubbed out.

how_it_breaks.language: Goes glossy and cute: God becomes a young woman, then a puppy.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Pencil turns to charcoal and smudge, then brown fog.

how_it_breaks.language: Draws everyday photos instead: children doing homework, a bowl of food.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Goes stark black and white, then a dark silhouette in green static.

how_it_breaks.language: Hangs on to faint sketches longest, then draws people instead.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Lines thin out, then splatter like spilled ink.

how_it_breaks.language: The most fragile: a few percent off and the page turns to flat colour.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Breaks into speckled noise within a quarter.

how_it_breaks.language: Ink turns to abstract paint, embers and frost.
how_it_breaks.drawing: Lines thin and fade until the page is nearly empty.

not_in_zoo: Muse Image, Meta's image AI, is used only through Meta's API: there are no weights to open, so it can't be damaged this way. Meta's open Muse Glimmer was damaged instead (/plato/glimmer).
